units.title: The last day of the Holm contract.
units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Today is the last day of the contract. I would like this to be the only thread about it, please. Observations, sources, and guesses clearly labelled as guesses. I will remind everyone that the people on that island have families, some of whom read this board, so please write as though they are reading. Thank you.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: 07:00 at Carrow Point: 1030 hPa and easing, wind SE 4, visibility 35 km, frost. As for the Holm's skyline: I won't pretend to count trees at nine kilometres. The south end looks lower than I remember it. The north ridge still shows a dark line. I'm a weatherman, not a forester, so take that for what it is.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: My prediction, since we are at the end: the contract ends today on paper, the crew come off in the next day or two in daylight on the contractor's own boat, and the arguments about the invoice begin. If the work isn't finished, a second contract will be let quietly in the spring. Land speculation is patient. I shall be glad to be told I'm wrong next week.

units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: On a day like this I find myself thinking of the clerk's last entries in the 1890s camp diary, now transcribed on the society wiki. I would ask that nobody draw parallels. It was a different camp, with different tools, in a different century, and the parish registers show no deaths that winter, whatever else they don't show.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: And if they don't come off in a day or two? I've asked that every day for a week and nobody answers, because nobody knows. The owners haven't given one date. Look at the property list, even the parts that held up: remote, self-contained, nothing around them. I'm not saying refuge any more. I'm saying ask.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Gil, in one week you have said refuge, then planted, then 'not saying refuge'. I don't mind members changing their minds; most of us should do it more often. I would only ask that you say so plainly when you do, so that others can follow.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: I went down to the Lisle slip this morning to watch the workboat go past, which I have never done for any boat in my life. Several others were there too, pretending to walk dogs. My former pupils on the morning ferry say it went out low and came back low. I take that to mean there was more to bring back than to take. I may be wrong.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: The school has asked parents not to talk about 'the island' at the gate because the younger ones are getting upset. My youngest asked me at breakfast whether the tree people have a lamp. I said I'm sure they do, lots of them. Is that true? I'd like it to be true.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: I have put a second lamp in the back bedroom window, the one that faces the island. I dont say they need it. My mother would have done it, I think, so I have. If anyone from the island reads this board, the house at the top of Kirk Brae is awake, and will be.

units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: Ferrous is probably right about the spring. If theyre not done theyll let a mop-up job, two men and a chipper for a month. Ive put my name down with the agency, just in case. Not that I want to go out there. I said I was glad I didnt go and I still am. I just know where the work is.

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: For anyone wondering about the council's position after today: no notice is required when works end, and none will be issued. If the owner applies for anything further, it will appear on the weekly list, which I read every Friday, and I will post it with the reference. Until then there is nothing to read, and I'd suggest nobody reads anything into nothing.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: I'll keep my lamp lit. That's all I've got to say on it, and all I'm going to.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: Course they've got lamps. They've got generators, floodlights, the lot. It's a work camp, not a shipwreck. Honestly, you lot, tell the kid the truth: they're fine and bored.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: Low out, low back, and Bram says fuel still going out yesterday. Someone tell me how that adds up to 'finished'. I'll be on the harbour wall tomorrow at six with a camera, and I'll post whatever I see, boat or no boat.

units.author: morrow_unknown
units.text: Kirk Brae's lamp is lit. I can see it from my window, and the one by the chapel, and most of the harbour front. I don't think I've ever seen so many. The island's lights are on too. I'm going to stop posting for a while. Sorry. Thank you for letting me read.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: Don't apologise. Reading counts for a great deal. I'll be up, as ever, for anyone who wants company, here or on the other board. The shop lamp is on, and the kettle, and there is a chair by the window.

units.title: Council newsletter: 'back to normal'.
units.author: sb_bins
units.text: Yesterday's council newsletter says collections are 'back to normal across the district'. For once I agree with the council newsletter, and I have written to tell them so, which I expect will confuse the waste team considerably. The heron photograph is also very good. Bernard (Rope Walk)

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Bernard, the heron was taken by my neighbour's grandson, who will be delighted to hear it has your approval. I shall frame this post for the board's archive. Nobody will believe it otherwise.

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: Weyhaven's newsletter says the same and our bins went yesterday on the wrong side of the road, so they took the odd numbers twice and the even numbers not at all. Normal, I suppose. That is normal.

units.title: Are the night outages over, then?
units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Genuine question, not a wind-up. We had a planned cut this morning on Mill Lane, off 09:02 to 12:41, which was early, well done them. But nothing at night for a week. Is that it? Can I stop keeping the freezer full of ice blocks and the torches on the stairs? The kids want their stair torch back for a den.

units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: Can confirm the Brackwater junction streetlight is working for the first time since the temp lights went in. Also the industrial estate unloaded my van in the dark tonight for the first time in a fortnight. Nobody stood in the doorway watching. Small wins.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: I'm on days now, so this is from the depot board: no trips logged on the coastal feeders since the 25th. The new insulators are in. I asked to move to day work and they said yes, so I don't patrol nights any more. I still can't explain the two no-fog nights, and nobody at the depot can either. We just stopped getting them. Keep a torch on the stairs anyway; it's winter.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: My station agrees with Tess on the fog: none recorded on two of the trip nights, and the salt deposit on my sensor shield those weeks was normal for the season. I'm not saying it wasn't corrosion. I'm saying it wasn't fog. Evening reading, while I'm here: 1028 hPa, falling slowly, cloud arriving from the south tomorrow.

units.title: Ferries & Roads: winter timetable from the 3rd.
units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: For fellow Lisle commuters: the winter timetable starts on the 3rd and the first boat moves to 07:15, which gives me five extra minutes in bed and five fewer at my desk. No Sunday night crossing until spring. This month the 07:10 was late eleven times, on time nineteen. I keep a notebook. I'm aware of how that sounds.

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: For those asking: the 22:40 runs on weekdays and Saturdays all winter, with the floodlights. I'm on it through December. Eleven late out of thirty in a month like this one I'd call respectable, but I'll pass your notebook on to the office.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Respectable is fair. I spoke to your first mate on the way home last week and I've stopped being sarcastic about the welfare review. I'll keep the notebook, though. Somebody has to, and it's easier than thinking about anything else on that crossing.

units.author: sb_lostcat
units.text: Small Pebble progress: she went out at dusk tonight and sat on the garden wall for ten whole minutes, looking at the street, then came in by herself and asked for her supper. I am counting this as a triumph. Thank you all for your patience with a woman and her cat.

units.author: gilliver_teen
units.text: glasses collected by Bram's brother, who tipped me a pound and told me I'd 'turned out alright in the end'. not sure what he means by in the end. I'm taking it though

units.author: propwatch_ledger
units.text: A final note on this thread. I have written to the registry asking for the full transfer history of entry 4, the one that still looks most like the Holm purchase. Replies take months. I won't post again about Ardent Vale until I hear back, and I will post the reply whatever it says, including if it says I was wrong.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: This thread has run its course. I am locking it, with thanks to propwatch for the corrections and the patience. New filings belong in a new thread, with references, please. Speculation without filings belongs nowhere I moderate.

units.title: The Lisle school roof (a correction to the Courier).
units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: The Courier quoted 'a former teacher' on the Lisle school roof. That was me. I said it leaked in the same place in 1991, which is true; I did not say we were 'promised a new one', I said we were promised a survey, which is what we got. A small difference, but I taught the difference between a promise and a survey for a living.

units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: The society holds the 1991 survey, as it happens, donated with the school's logbooks. It recommends 'replacement within five years'. So the roof is twenty-nine years late by the surveyor's own estimate. I shall add this to the Lisle school article with a straight face.

units.title: End of the month: roll call
units.author: lh_mod
units.text: Housekeeping: month end. A roll call for anyone who wants one: where you are, what the night is like, one good thing. Keep it kind and short-ish. And thank you, genuinely, for a long month. Water, then bed, when you're done.

units.author: lh_baker_coriveth
units.text: Coriveth harbour bakery, cold and clear, the ovens ticking as they warm. Good thing: the Inspector sat on the step tonight and let me look at his leg. It's an old injury, healed crooked, and he's perfectly fine. Brioche for the weekend.

units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: Container port, east gate. 00:00 patrol, nil found. Wind light, sky clear. Good thing: the day shift left me a flask of soup with a note on it. First note in four years. Logged.

units.author: lh_carer_vellmark
units.text: Vellmark, the home on the hill. Nine residents asleep and one awake doing a jigsaw of a lighthouse with me. The intercom has been quiet since our resident passed, and we keep her chair by the window. Good thing: the jigsaw has all its pieces. Sorry, that was long.

units.author: lh_crane_halvard
units.text: Halvard, 60 m up, frost on the cab glass. Good thing: the site manager brought hot rolls up the tower at midnight. He's afraid of heights. He came anyway, and he didn't look down once.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Halvard sleep clinic: four patients wired up and asleep, plus one very polite sleepwalker. Good thing: one patient slept six straight hours for the first time in a year. I'd like to take the credit. It was mostly the new pillow.

units.author: lh_nurse_halvard
units.text: Respiratory ward, Halvard: nine of twelve beds, everyone breathing, which is the job. Good thing: a man going home tomorrow taught the night sister a card trick and she's been practising it on the drug trolley all night. Back to it.

units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: Port Ammet General, the run. Good thing: they've fixed the bulb on the car park steps, fourth time lucky. Last night of nights for me. My mate who used to cut trees came in to see his mum on the ward and said, out of nowhere, 'hope they get off that island soon'. Then he went quiet again.

units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: Weyhaven retail park, route C, car park nearly empty. Good thing: Control has given me the weekend off, unprompted, with a 'well done', which may be a sign of the end times or just a new manager.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: Tollinby, the flat above the bookshop, a lamp in the window. Good thing: someone left a note under the shop door asking me to put aside a book about lighthouses for her daughter. I've put three aside. I'll let the daughter choose.

units.author: lh_miner_vellmark
units.text: Vellmark, end of shift, on the bus. Good thing: nobody hurt this month. That's the only good thing that counts down there. Frost on the pit-head and a clear sky.

units.author: lh_callcentre_tamsin
units.text: Tamsin Bay helpline, start of shift. Good thing: last night Gerald rang at 01:17 as usual and I said 'evening, Gerald' out loud, and my team lead laughed for the first time since the restructure. Small victories, between calls.

units.author: lh_lighttender_tamsin
units.text: Tamsin Bay light: a clear sky full of stars and the beam going round like a slow clock. Good thing: a fishing boat flashed me a hello on her way in, and I flashed back. The gallery door is shut. The kettle is on. Thank you all for the company this month.

units.title: I kept a tally of the edge-of-light posts (please be gentle)
units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: Because I can't sleep, I went through the merged thread and made a list, the way the Dellow gentleman does with footsteps. Twenty-four reports. Seven withdrawn or explained by the posters themselves: a fox, a man waiting for a lift, a sleeping driver, a runner, a faulty camera, and two 'probably tired'. Seventeen left. I don't know what seventeen means. I just wanted it written down by someone who doesn't mind either way.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Thank you; that's honest work. Seventeen unexplained out of twenty-four, from tired people on a forum that talks about exactly this, is roughly what I'd predict from reporting effects alone. That doesn't prove I'm right. It means seventeen is not, by itself, evidence of anything.

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: And of the seventeen, how many came within a week of someone else's report? I'd bet most of them. That's the contagion I keep banging on about. Not a criticism of your list, which is lovely. It's a criticism of all of us, me and my phone lines included.

units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: Confirmed: mine is in the seven (fox). Thank you for checking with the posters rather than guessing on their behalf. That's proper procedure, and more than most incident reviews manage.

units.author: lh_mod
units.text: Housekeeping: with the poster's permission I'm pinning this list in the merged thread and closing both threads to new reports tonight. Not because anything has been decided. Because a month is long enough for any thread, and most of you need sleep more than another report.

units.author: lh_miner_vellmark
units.text: Seventeen. Old lads would say that's seventeen people who stayed in the light. Which is the point of the light. Bus is here.

units.author: lh_lighttender_tamsin
units.text: Mine was one of the first, I think, before anyone else's that week, so it may spoil Orla's sum a little. I have no wish to defend it. I count myself among the seventeen, and I would still much rather be explained than believed.

units.title: The van, one last time
units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: For anyone who remembers the van that idled four hours at the edge of the car park lights with nobody in the cab, and later turned up at the Brackwater junction: I asked Control to run the plate. It's registered to a hire company that went bust in the spring. So nobody owns it, and nobody's reported it. I've stopped looking. I'm telling you so it's written down somewhere.

units.author: lh_baker_coriveth
units.text: Our second van, the one that parked at the edge of the streetlight and never ran its engine, has gone. Not seen for a week. The street feels bigger without it. I don't think I'll miss it, and I don't want to know whose it was.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Vans from bust hire firms end up everywhere: people buy them at auction and never re-register them. An empty cab for four hours is a driver asleep in the back, or in a café across the road. Unexciting, probable, unprovable. Like most things.

units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: Probably. I did check the back that night, through the rear window with my torch, and it was empty. But probably. I'll take probably, and the weekend off.

units.author: lh_kennel_orrin
units.text: Thanks, all. Pepper went home today with her family, wagging. The new route works fine. The boss has turned the back corridor into storage, so nobody has to walk it at all. Problem solved, in the dumbest possible way, which is my favourite way.

units.title: Coffee report, last night of the month
units.author: lh_trucker_orrin
units.text: Coffee report for the prairie: the lit stop at milepost 212 has a new machine that grinds the beans, and it's the best cup on the route. Took my rest there under the floodlights like a sensible person. Clear, cold, no wind, stars right down to the ground. Drive safe, all of you, wherever your road is.

units.author: lh_kennel_orrin
units.text: 212 is twenty minutes from us. If you're ever passing in daylight, the clinic has a dog who will sell you his soul for a corner of a sandwich. His name is Bruno. He has no shame.

units.title: chapter submitted
units.author: lh_student_kestrel
units.text: chapter submitted. 11,400 words. I cried a bit in the lift. the corridor lights came on for me tonight as I walked out, one by one, which is exactly what they're supposed to do, and it was honestly the nicest thing they've ever done for me. going to sleep for a day

units.author: lh_convenience_kestrel
units.text: Congratulations. Come by the shop on your way home and I'll give you a steamed bun on the house. The forecourt man was there again tonight. He bought one. I think it's because I told him about you.

units.title: Residents' meeting: short minutes
units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: Short minutes, 14 attending. (1) Lift seal: Kerrow say next week. (2) Chiller removal: agreed, date to follow, Hassan to help. (3) Roof door: reported again, Kerrow to check the lock. (4) Stairwell: the lights are working; several residents still prefer the lift at night, which is their choice. No further action. (5) Christmas: party in the community room, Lorna and Irena volunteering. Bev, DCRA

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: Fourteen people at a meeting about a light bulb. Weyhaven never changes.

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Thank you for item (4). For the record, I said at the meeting that I've stopped counting and I'm not starting again. My last figure was 41 steps for a descent of 38. I don't stand behind it as proof of anything. I stand behind it as a count.

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: About item (2): as I said, the bin store chiller is the shop's and it was switched off. I checked the plug myself on the 27th. I am glad it is going. It was not making the noise. I do not know what was.

units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: Fourteen people at a meeting about their homes, actually, and you don't live here. Please be nicer, or post somewhere else. Bev, DCRA

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: item 4 noted, item 5 is a vibe. i'll bring the speaker. not playing anything about stairs. ok maybe one song about stairs, as a treat

units.author: dc_14_ivy
units.text: (Item 5 is the best item.) I'll draw the party poster if Bev wants: a tree with lights on it the whole height of the building, fourteen floors. No stairwell in it, I promise. Possibly a roof door, very firmly shut.

units.author: dc_10_garrick
units.text: Item 5: I'll run a sponsored stair climb for the party fund, ground to 14 and back, in daylight, on a Saturday, so nobody can blame me for any footsteps. Sign-up sheet on my door. Legends only.

units.title: A short note from 7C
units.author: dc_7_irena
units.text: Dear neighbours, a short note. I took the stairs this morning, in daylight, from 7 down to 6, with Lorna holding my arm. Nothing happened, which is as it should be. I did not hear anything, and I was glad. I do not say it is over. I only say that I have done it once, and that once is enough for this month. Irena, 7C

units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: we did it love, one flight and a cup of tea after, and she counted the steps out loud the whole way down just to annoy Tobin, which I thought was very good of her, eighteen steps, for anyone keeping a list

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: Well done, both of you. Free loaf for Irena and Lorna on Friday, and the good biscuits, not the broken ones. H

units.title: Notice: removal of refrigeration unit, level 8 bin store
units.author: dellow_manager
units.text: Kerrow Estates notice ref DC/BIN/0419. The removal of the redundant refrigeration unit from the level 8 bin store has been scheduled. Residents will be notified of the date in due course. Residents are asked not to place refuse or other items in front of the unit in the meantime. We thank residents for their patience.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: For the record, since I claimed vindication on the 26th when this unit was found: unplugged means unplugged. Whatever people recorded on 8, it wasn't this compressor. I was too quick. One line, as usual, and then I'll leave it.

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: I'll be there with the sack truck when they come. That chiller has been unplugged since the spring, I'll say it again. It was a good chiller once. It held the milk for nine years. H

units.author: dellow_manager
units.text: Kerrow Estates notice ref DC/ROOF/0420. The roof access door has been inspected and the lock found to be functioning correctly. No evidence of unauthorised access has been identified. Residents are reminded that the roof is not a communal area.

units.author: dc_14_ivy
units.text: 'Functioning correctly.' (It was open on Tuesday morning; Ollie saw it.) Both things can apparently be true at Kerrow. I'm drawing the roof door for the party poster anyway, shut, with a bow on it.

units.title: Holm landing stage: after today
units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: Notice: the contractor's vessel loaded and sailed at 06:35 this morning as booked, and has returned. Berth 3 is released from tomorrow. I have had no further booking and no notification of further movements to the Holm. If one arrives I will post it here. I would ask members, kindly, not to fill the gap with guesses. Thank you.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: Their workboat's skipper had a coffee with us at Gilliver this morning. He says he's 'on standby from tomorrow, waiting to hear'. He hasn't been told a date either. Not his fault. Contractors' boats are never told anything until the night before, in my experience.

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: We passed the Holm on the 13:00 run. Their boat was back at Gilliver by then, tied up. Smoke from what I took for a fire on the south shoulder. Nothing more to say than that. Logged it, carried on.

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: Same from the deck. Lights on at the camp at dusk yesterday from the 17:00. Somebody's there and working. That is the only thing about that island I'd put my name to, and I'm putting it.

units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: Ha... I keep looking at it from the bakery window between customers. My manager has noticed. It looks the same as it did, and also different. I don't know how to say that better, sorry.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: Quill's right lads. No booking no boat. When there's a boat there'll be a notice. Chandlery open Saturday as normal if anyone needs owt for their own boat. Lamp oil's sold out, before anyone asks.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Creels on the Holm side this morning. Saw folk on the shore at the yard end, working. Waved. One of them waved back. That's all.

units.author: gilliver_teen
units.text: not trolling. just saying the whole harbour front is lit tonight, like every window. my nan put two on. even the chippy's got one in the window now, the boss did it this afternoon without saying anything to anyone

units.title: Heights (once more, for the record, sorry)
units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: I know. But I'm putting it down once more for the record, since Ada's at the bakery and won't be posting much. Mine on the 4th: tall, over six foot, I'd say six four, judged against the bollard. Ada's at Lisle on the 10th she put at average, five eight or so. We don't agree. We're not going to agree. Both of us stand by what we said.

units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: I do stand by it... five eight, maybe five nine. It was drizzly and I was a long way off. Ha. Maybe it was two different... no. I'm not saying that. I'm saying we each saw what we saw, differently, and I'd sooner leave it there.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: Fair enough Kerris. Record's straight now. That's the last heights thread on here lads, the next one goes to the Sound Board or nowhere.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: As a retired surveyor: judging a height at 40 m in drizzle against a bollard of known size, I'd allow four inches either way. At 80 m with no reference, eight. Your two figures don't overlap even then. So either two different people, or one estimate is out. I don't know which. Nobody does, and nobody will.

units.author: gilliver_teen
units.text: for what it's worth I'm five ten and the coat made me look bigger, apparently. but that was the 7th, not the 4th or the 10th. I keep saying. I'm not either of them

units.title: Fuel berth hours this weekend
units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: Fuel berth open 07:00 to 16:00 Saturday, closed Sunday. Diesel up two cents from Monday's delivery. Don't shoot the messenger lads, I only sell it.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Up again. Grand. I'll fill on Saturday before it goes up again Monday, the way it always does when the weather's good.

units.title: Group session files: catalogue numbers assigned
units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: The Brackwater group session files (days 13 to 20) now have catalogue numbers LBA-2190 to 2206, with kit and gain as reported. The voice-like event in tern_audio's file is LBA-2197 at 31:44, described as 'tonal, about 1.1 s, unattributed'. dunlin_rec's incomplete file from the 24th is LBA-2208, 'ends abruptly'. Corrections welcome. No interpretations, please.

units.author: brackwater_keeper
units.text: For your catalogue: the estate's view is that nobody should be in those woods after dark recording anything. I said deer early on. I was wrong about deer. I've nothing better to offer. Keep your sessions to daylight and I'll leave the gate open for you.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so thanks for doing this. 2197 at 31:44 is right. I still don't know what it is. I've listened maybe two hundred times and it changes depending on how tired I am, which tells you something about me, not about the file.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: For the catalogue record: I proposed water hammer in the reservoir outflow for the Brackwater knocks. I withdrew it for the tonal event in 2197 on the 18th. I still stand by water hammer as a candidate for some of the knocks, not all of them. That's where I've landed.

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: A note for 2193, mine, the binaural rig at the stile: I walked back my 'above and behind' placement on the 18th after testing reflections in my own stairwell. Please add that to the entry so nobody quotes the old claim. Headphones off, conscience clear.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Thanks for cataloguing these properly. The description of 2208 is accurate as it stands. I'd rather not add anything to it.

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: Pinning the catalogue post. That's the end of the session threads for this year. Thank you all for posting raw files and admitting where you were wrong. That's rarer than knocks, and worth more.

units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Last word for now: re-recorded the same spot yesterday, same rig, same tide state, same gain. No hum at all. Whatever it was isn't there any more, so I can't find it to check it. Still a pump, in my book. Somebody's, somewhere, switched off.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: A source that's gone can't be tested, so it stays unattributed. That's the honest catalogue answer. Put it in the archive with the spectrum and the date, and leave the next person a clean starting point.

units.title: A tape for the end of the month (no knocks whatsoever)
units.author: hobby_tapeloop
units.text: Dear all, I have digitised a reel from the 1960s: Gilliver harbour on a summer evening, a fiddle at the pub door, a dog, gulls and the ferry horn twice. No knocks whatsoever. The tape hiss is magnificent. I offer it as a palate cleanser after a long month. Regards, Ned

units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: Catalogued as LBA-2225, with thanks. I've noted the recorder speed from the hiss profile, and that the fiddle is slightly flat, which I'm told is traditional. A lovely thing to end the month on.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Lovely. Thank you, Ned. I listened to it twice with the lights on and the window open. It's the best thing I've heard this month. Make of that what you will.
